- When sentiment is positive (≥0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast for next 3–5 days at 10–15% below peak.
- If history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days trending down), model tends to ignore it; adjust forecast downward by 2–5% per day of trend.
- When sentiment is neutral or negative (0.0), model often underestimates; add 3–7% to forecast if recent 5-day average is below 70.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overestimates early in the forecast (first 5–7 days); apply a 2–5% downward bias to first 7 days if sentiment is flat or negative.
- If sentiment history shows a sudden shift to positive (e.g., 0.0 → 0.5+), model often fails to adjust quickly; delay peak forecast by 1–2 days and reduce magnitude by 5–10%.
